title: Investor Type Quiz
subtitle: 10-step survey to find your investing style
intro: Answer 10 questions on horizon, loss tolerance, experience, and goals. We classify you into one of 10 investor types and suggest asset mix, market weights, and stock styles.
disclaimer: For education only — not investment advice. You can apply results to portfolio target weights in the app.
applyPrefsHint: Review under My Info → Capital & simulation
ctaBanner: Find your investor type with our 10-step quiz

horizon.title: Time horizon
horizon.question: How long can you keep money invested in stocks?

loss-tolerance.title: Loss tolerance
loss-tolerance.question: If your portfolio fell 20%, what would you do?

experience.title: Experience
experience.question: How much stock/ETF investing experience do you have?

income-stability.title: Income stability
income-stability.question: How stable is your main income?

emergency-fund.title: Emergency fund
emergency-fund.question: Do you have 6+ months of living expenses saved separately?

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.question: How well do you understand P/E, dividends, ETFs, diversification?

ultra-safe.name: Ultra conservative
ultra-safe.summary: Capital preservation first. Minimize stocks; favor cash and bonds.
warnings: Do not force high stock weights

safe.name: Conservative
safe.summary: Balance safety and modest return. Defensive ETFs and quality dividends.

conservative.name: Moderately conservative
conservative.summary: Keep bond/ETF weight while slowly adding stocks.

mod-conservative.name: Balanced conservative
mod-conservative.summary: Growth with stability. Diversified ETFs plus quality stocks.

balanced.name: Balanced
balanced.summary: Even mix of KR/US stocks and ETFs. Market-level risk/return.

mod-growth.name: Balanced growth
mod-growth.summary: Slightly more growth and US exposure. Accept mid-term swings.

growth.name: Growth
growth.summary: Higher stock allocation. Long-term compounding with broad diversification.

agg-growth.name: Aggressive growth
agg-growth.summary: More US and growth. Higher return target with larger swings.
warnings: Single name over 50% is excessive risk

aggressive.name: Aggressive
aggressive.summary: Growth, themes, US-heavy. Accept volatility for return.
warnings: No living expenses or debt investing

ultra-aggressive.name: Ultra aggressive
ultra-aggressive.summary: Maximum equity/US tilt. Long-term high return; large drawdowns OK.

risk-check.title: Quick risk tolerance quiz
risk-check.subtitle: 5 questions on volatility and loss tolerance
risk-check.intro: Answer five questions on losses, crises, return expectations, emergency fund, and diversification.

tier-1.name: Very low
tier-1.summary: Capital preservation first. Favor cash and bonds; keep stocks minimal.

tier-2.name: Low
tier-2.summary: Small dips may feel stressful. Dividend ETFs and quality names in small size fit well.

tier-3.name: Moderate
tier-3.summary: You can accept some volatility. ETF + diversified stocks work well.

tier-4.name: High
tier-4.summary: You can ride mid-term drawdowns and buy in tranches. Growth/balance mix is OK.

tier-5.name: Very high
tier-5.summary: Large swings are OK, but avoid betting living expenses; strict risk rules still matter.

horizon-goal.title: Horizon & goal check
horizon-goal.subtitle: 5 questions on timeline, purpose, and readiness
horizon-goal.intro: Five questions on horizon, goals, experience, income, and knowledge.

tier-1.name: Short-term / preserve
tier-1.summary: Under 1 year or capital preservation — prefer deposits, CMA, short bonds over stocks.

tier-2.name: Medium / stable
tier-2.summary: 1–3 year goals — raise bonds and dividend ETF weight for safety.

tier-3.name: Mid-long / accumulate
tier-3.summary: 3–10 year savings fit regular stock/ETF DCA.

tier-4.name: Long / grow
tier-4.summary: 10+ year wealth building — can gradually raise equity weight.

tier-5.name: Very long / clear goal
tier-5.summary: Retirement-grade horizon — long diversification plus ISA/pension worth reviewing.

allocation-style.title: Allocation style quiz
allocation-style.subtitle: 5 questions on preferred asset mix
allocation-style.intro: Five questions on diversification, return, loss tolerance, purpose, and horizon.

tier-1.name: Cash & bonds core
tier-1.summary: Heavy cash, deposits, MMF, short bonds; minimal stocks.

tier-2.name: Bond & ETF mix
tier-2.summary: Bonds and dividend ETFs as core; stocks secondary.

tier-3.name: Balanced
tier-3.summary: Even mix of stocks, ETFs, cash — near 60/40 or 70/30.

tier-4.name: Equity & ETF growth
tier-4.summary: Higher stock/growth ETF weight while staying diversified.

tier-5.name: Concentrated equity
tier-5.summary: Higher single-stock/growth tilt — position limits and rules are essential.
